title: Vision-vs-Language SAE Sparsity Gap as a Monitoring Cost Signal

original_idea.body:
# Vision-vs-Language SAE Sparsity Gap as a Monitoring Cost Signal

**Problem:** Vision SAEs need far higher L0 than language SAEs; unclear what this means for SAE-based monitoring of multimodal models.

**Direction:** Using ViT-Prisma's pre-trained vision SAEs and a language SAE, map L0/monosemanticity vs the difficulty of finding a clean concept feature in vision vs language.

**Why it matters:** Multimodal monitoring may need different sparsity assumptions. Training-free.

**Relevant context:** Joseph et al. (arXiv 2504.19475).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (multimodal monitoring difficulty) but the safety-outcome link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses pre-trained Prisma SAEs, no training; guided though multimodal tooling adds friction.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused comparison (L0 vs concept-finding difficulty) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public weights, multimodal interp lags, lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on vision/language SAEs; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Vision-vs-language monitoring-cost framing seems largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The monitoring-cost framing of the vision/language sparsity gap appears largely unexplored.
